Harf bayraklarının yanında üç grup yardı.en: Besides the alphabetical flags there are three groups of auxiliary pennants. Numeral pennants (0–9) carry positions, times, channels and code-group numbers. Substitutes repeat a flag within the same hoist so that no second set is needed: a substitute repeats ONLY a flag of its own class (alphabetical or numeral). For example, 'ANNA' is hoisted as A-N-(second substitute)-(first substitute); the second substitute repeats the second flag of its class (N) and the first substitute repeats the first (A). With three substitutes, every four-character combination can be hoisted with a single set of flags. The answering pennant controls the flow of the exchange.

International Code of Signals (ICS), dil.en: The International Code of Signals (ICS) is a standard code designed to overcome language barriers, covering safety and navigation above all. With 26 alphabetical flags, 10 numeral pennants and the auxiliary pennants it conveys single-letter, two-letter and three-letter coded meanings. Messages can be sent by flag hoist, signalling lamp or sound.

International Code of Signals dil engeli.en: The International Code of Signals is the standard signal code that overcomes language barriers.

Tek harfli işaretler, ICS'in en acil ve.en: Single-letter signals are the most urgent and most frequently used part of the ICS, and every one of them should be known by heart. All 26 letters are given below. Some letters have a separate meaning when made by fishing vessels (G, P, Z) — the distinction most often confused in examinations and at sea.

Tek harfli işaretlerin ötesinde, emniyet.en: Beyond the single-letter signals, most safety and emergency messages are sent as two-letter groups. Whatever language the stations speak, the groups are read by their meaning in the ICS book.

Telsiz haberleşmesinin yanı sıra denizci.en: Besides radio communication, seafarers must know visual signalling methods so that they can still communicate during radio silence or a radio failure. The International Code of Signals standardises messages sent by flags, signalling lamp and sound.
